jobs.description_text: As civilization electrifies, energy demand will continue to outpace the deployment of terrestrial infrastructure required to deliver it. Building a system that has never existed requires people who are comfortable working where physics, engineering, manufacturing, and execution meet. It requires builders who are energized by difficult problems, move comfortably across disciplines, and measure progress by evidence. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern
jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is designed end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Mechanical Engineering Intern to design the structure that carries our ground beacon system, including transportation of the system from the lab to the field test. The beacon and its system components all have to travel together, set up fast, and stay co-located with our observational telescope. Portable, modular, and rigid are competing goals. You'll own that trade and defend it. Alongside the mounting, you'll characterize what the environment does to the installed system so we know how much of the pointing error budget the structure is spending. This internship supports our program under a Department of War energy investment program. You'll work directly with the optics team to ensure the structure design meets the optical beacon requirements. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design system mounting for three states: pre-delivery, in transit, and installed at the test site - Trade portability and modularity against stiffness and alignment retention, and document the reasoning behind the design you pick - Design a transportable platform to house beacon equipment - Build parametric CAD models and produce drawings a machine shop can quote and manufacture - Analyze environmental effects on the installed system, including temperature and wind loading, and quantify the impact on pointing stability - Characterize transportation effe

jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where the operating concept and every warfighter conversation helps to define how this technology is used. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Deployment Operations Intern to research what rules govern space solar energy operations, and how a warfighter actually operates the system. In support of a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program, you'll research the policy landscape for space and beacon operations and turn it into concrete CONOPS language. You'll research DoW sites for present and future testing, and you'll build the material that makes this technology legible to the people who would use it to feed our broader space solar energy operational guide. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Research U.S. policy and regulation governing space operations and ground-based beacon operations, and translate it into CONOPS language the engineering team can design against - Identify and profile DoW sites for present and future testing, including access, airspace, and environmental considerations - Support warfighter engagement: prepare briefing material, capture feedback in the room, and route it back into CONOPS and design - Draft an operator manual written for the warfighter, not the engineer - Create warfighter and DoW engagement materials that make an unfamiliar technology easy to understand quickly - Track DoW expectations against what we're producing, and flag gaps early WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR FROM YOU - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program

jobs.title: Optics Intern
jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is aligned, characterized, and field-corrected end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Optics Intern to help with the design and building of our ground beacon from the optical bench to a field test site. The beacon is the pointing reference the satellite system will depend on. If it isn't aligned and characterized correctly, nothing downstream works. You'll work hands-on with the emitter and the observational telescope: aligning the laser, characterizing its output, and co-aligning the beacon with the telescope. Then you'll own a problem we haven't solved yet. Once the system is transported to the test site, alignment may shift. You'll design the procedure that brings it back. This internship supports our program under a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program. You'll work alongside our optics and hardware engineers, and your alignment data will feed directly into hardware decisions we make. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Align the beacon laser within its emitter and verify pointing outside the emitter aperture - Characterize laser output - power, beam profile, divergence, and pointing stability - and document the results - Co-align the beacon laser with the observational telescope and verify boresight - Design a repeatable field alignment procedure that corrects misalignment introduced during transport and installation at the DoW site - Write that procedure so a n

You will fix real vulnerabilities when they appear, then change the underlying systems so the same class of issue is harder to introduce again. ABOUT YOU: Have deep intuition on application security, software architecture, and how vulnerabilities emerge in real systems. You are comfortable finding issues yourself, but care more about eliminating vulnerability classes through better libraries, frameworks, and defaults. You still like to write production code and have strong opinions on where current AI models are useful for security work and where they mostly create noise. You are comfortable operating independently, prioritizing the highest-leverage problems, and working directly with both engineers and customers. jobs.title: Research Engineer - Post-Training
jobs.description_text: Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Build the post-training stack: You build the RL training loop end-to-end: rollout ingestion from the geo-distributed inference pipeline, reward computation, policy updates, and getting updated weights back out to the network. You set the direction, and you make things happen. - Invent the algorithms: Standard RL recipes assume on-policy rollouts from fast, trusted hardware. You adapt them to asynchronous, high-latency, partially trusted generation: staleness tolerance, off-policy corrections, and communication-efficient policy updates. - Ship first post-trained models: You build the evals that show the models are improving, and you take the first decentralized post-trained release from run to public artifact. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Hands-on distributed training (required): You've trained models across many devices in PyTorch with FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron, or your own implementation. jobs.title: Research Engineer - Geo-Distributed Inference
jobs.description_text: Our inference pipeline generates the rollouts for reinforcement learning (RL) training today, and it'll serve our models once they're trained. It also runs in a permissionless, trustless setting, which makes the usual serving problem much harder. The hardware is Macs and consumer GPUs owned by strangers, the network is the public internet, nodes join and leave mid-run, and the weights change under the server as training moves. Your primary role is to build the systems that keep this pipeline fast and reliable under these conditions. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the inference stack: You build and own it end-to-end. Pipeline-parallel execution, placement and routing, the transport, the serving engine, and failure handling. You set the direction, and you make things happen. - Invent the algorithms: Making inference fast on consumer hardware over the public internet takes methods that don't exist yet. You design them, validate them, and put them in production. - Serve training and users: You keep the rollout pipeline fast and reliable for RL training now, and turn it into the serving layer for our models once they're trained. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Shipped serving systems: You've shipped serving-engine internals or built a large-scale inference system yourself, and you can do this work hands-on today. - Research ability: Publications (papers and blogposts) in distributed inference or a nearby field, such as LLM serving systems, pipeline parallelism over slow networks, or decentra

jobs.title: Research Engineer - Decentralized Training and Inference Verification
jobs.description_text: Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system. An inference worker can return tokens from a cheaper model, or a highly quantized version of the one it's supposed to run. Even with the right model, it can sample with the wrong parameters. Training faces its own attacks, and Agora showed what a permissionless run deals with in practice: participants who disrupt training by dropping updates or flooding the system, free-riders who submit trivial work and collect the rewards, poisoned updates that plant backdoors, attempts to extract private data from gradients and activations, and contributors who inflate their reported work to claim rewards they didn't earn. Sentinel https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03592 is our first published answer on the training side. Your primary role is to come up with efficient algorithms and systems that verify the work: that tokens came from the claimed model and sampling parameters, and that training contributions are what they claim to be. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the threat model: You enumerate what a malicious or careless worker can do across pre-training, post-training, and inference — training disruption and denial-of-service, free-riding, model poisoning and backdoors, data extraction from gradients and activations, reputation and reward manipulation — and you keep that model current as the network grows. - Design and calibrate the tests: You build statis

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Pylon is looking for a Customer Success Manager to be the face of Pylon for our customers, the person they turn to as they onboard, ramp up, and get real value out of the product. You'll own a book of accounts end to end: hosting calls, answering questions, teaching best practices, and making sure every customer actually uses what they're paying for. This is a hands-on, in-person role at a fast-growing company, and a rare seat where your day-to-day feedback directly shapes our product roadmap. What You'll Do - Own onboarding and adoption for your book of customers: host calls, answer questions in real time, and teach best practices so customers get value fast. - Keep customers current on new features through creative, scalable channels, webinars, written content, office hours, whatever actually gets the message across. - Watch usage and engagement signals closely, and proactively reach out to customers who aren't using the product as expected before it becomes a bigger problem. - Partner with engineering to build the tooling and internal processes that make customer success more efficient as we grow, and turn what you hear from customers into real product feedback. - Dogfood Pylon for your own workflows every day. You're not just a user of the product, you're one of the people shaping what we build next. REQUIREMENTS - 0-2 years of experience in a Customer Success, Account Management, or other customer-facing role (new grads welcome). - BA/BS degree or equivale

jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE You will be our first dedicated engineering leader, reporting to the CTO with a direct line to both founders - no layers in between. Today, engineering at Prior Labs is a small, very senior team. We plan to grow it substantially over the next 18 months, and your job is to build and run that organization. We want to be honest about what this job is. It is a hands-on operator role: managing engineers, building the hiring machine, setting standards, running compliance, and working closely with our partners at SAP. If you light up at making an organization fast rather than at owning the biggest possible headcount, this is your role. What you'll do - Directly manage and grow the engineering team, including building out its management layer. - Build the hiring machine: run hiring operations across our hiring managers, design interview loops that hold up in the AI era, and keep a very high bar while the team grows. - Own engineering standards and velocity: how we review, test, and ship - and how the team gets real leverage from AI coding tools. - Own our security and compliance program - SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001 - right-sized, so the lab keeps its speed. - Own the engineering side of our collaboration with SAP. - Treat the deployment layer as a product surface: our models reach customers through a managed API, customer VPCs, and self-hosted open weights, and the engineering behind that needs customer empathy, not just platform craft. - Act as a sparring partner to the founder

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Integrations
jobs.description_text: The role Most enterprises will never call our API directly. They will meet TabPFN inside the platforms they already run: SAP, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Databricks, or their own cloud. How well that works, how fast each release arrives there, and which platforms come next is the job of our Technical Product Manager for Integrations. You take each model release from handover to live across every channel, working with the engineers who build the model and the partner teams who host it. Inside SAP you carry the product side of TabPFN across its platforms, from AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud, and you help build the integration engineering team that will work with you. Several decisions are yours to bring to the table: which announced channels we build next, what a marketplace listing should cost, how support for all of this works. You work directly with our product team, our engineers and the founders, and you report to the CTO. This suits someone who enjoys landing things on a date as much as deciding what to build, and who still likes being close to the code. What you'll do - Take every model release live across SAP, the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, on a plan you build with product and engineering. - Be the technical counterpart for the partner teams that host TabPFN, from SAP's platform teams to the hyperscaler marketplaces. - Shape how TabPFN shows up inside SAP's stack and what the integration engineering team builds first. - Bring the open channel decisions

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, AI Infrastructure
jobs.description_text: Senior Product Manager, Infrastructure, Scaling & Core Workflow Primitives Transform healthcare with us. JOB SUMMARY Qualified Health is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own how the platform compounds: the core workflow primitives that every product is assembled from, the builder tools that let teams create assistants, abstractors, and workflows, and the scaling discipline that turns one-off builds into products that generalize. Builder tools are the velocity engine of our platform. This role makes the engine compound: a component built once for one application becomes a primitive available to every application after it. This is a three-prong role. Second, make sure products ship scalable, not as one-offs: generalization requirements are set before build, and the second customer costs a fraction of the first.
